lines.text: The jury awarded seven hundred thousand dollars, but the opinion divided that number into two different accounts with different recipients and different injuries.
Two hundred thousand dollars was assessed on the decedent's account and made payable to the heirs, tied to her own hours of suffering.
Five hundred thousand dollars addressed the survivors' pain, suffering, and mental anguish: three children and four grandchildren named by category.
The evidence described her as the family hub, and one witness called her the trunk of the family tree.
The hospital challenged the damages after trial, but it had not preserved the legal theory in the required pretrial order or directed-verdict motion.
The panel called that move locking the barn door long after the horse had bolted: the argument arrived after the procedural chance to make it.
The court ordered no remittitur, reversed nothing, and left the jury's assessment intact without deciding every broader question the case raised.
The total therefore returns to its two parts: her account for the wait, and the family's separate suffering after losing its center.
